cameras.label: DJI Zenmuse H20 wide camera
cameras.name: Zenmuse H20 wide camera
cameras.notes: An inspection payload: usable for mapping, but the 12 MP wide camera gives a coarse ground resolution.

cameras.label: DJI Mini 4 Pro camera (48 MP)
cameras.name: Mini 4 Pro camera (48 MP)
cameras.notes: 48 MP stills write slowly: the longer minimum interval limits flight speed.

cameras.label: MicaSense RedEdge-MX (per band)
cameras.name: RedEdge-MX (per band)
cameras.notes: Multispectral: 1.2 MP per band, so the same altitude gives a much coarser ground resolution than an RGB mapping camera.

drones.label: DJI Mini 4 Pro

formats.note: DJI Fly has no import button: the file replaces a placeholder mission saved on the controller. DJI Fly does not run interval triggers from the file, so either start interval shooting on the camera before the mission or export with a photo at every waypoint.

drones.notes: A sub-250 g aircraft: wind tolerance and endurance in cold weather are well below the rated figures.

drones.label: DJI Air 2S
drones.notes: DJI Fly has no waypoint flight on this model; missions are flown with a third-party app.

drones.label: DJI Mini 3
drones.notes: DJI Fly offers no waypoint flight on this model. The plan can still be used as a reference for a manually flown grid.

drones.label: DJI Matrice 350 RTK
drones.notes: The 55 min endurance is without a payload; the endurance factor allows for a Zenmuse P1-class payload. Service ceiling 5000 m with standard propellers.

drones.label: Generic PX4 / ArduPilot multirotor
drones.notes: A starting point, not a real aircraft: copy it to a custom profile and enter your airframe's measured endurance and speeds.

drones.label: Wingtra WingtraOne GEN II
drones.notes: WingtraPilot plans the flight lines itself from an imported area. The 5000 m ceiling needs high-altitude propellers; ground wind limit for takeoff and landing is lower than the cruise limit.

ecosystems.help: Imports WPML route files (.kmz). Needs the aircraft's DJI WPML id.

ecosystems.help: DJI Fly has no import; a WPML file replaces a saved mission on the controller. Needs the aircraft's DJI WPML id.

ecosystems.help: Loads QGroundControl plans and MAVLink waypoint lists.
ecosystems.label: PX4 / ArduPilot (QGroundControl, Mission Planner)

ecosystems.help: Imports waypoint CSV files through Litchi Mission Hub; 99 waypoints per mission.

ecosystems.help: No mission file can be exported; the plan is a reference.
ecosystems.label: No autonomous flight (flown by hand)

formats.description: Waypoint route for DJI Pilot 2 and FlightHub 2 (Enterprise aircraft). DJI Fly's Waypoint Flight reads the same format, but only by replacing a saved mission file on the controller.
instructions: DJI Pilot 2: copy the .kmz to the controller (microSD or USB), open Flight Route > Import Route (KMZ/KML) and pick the file. Check the aircraft, payload and every waypoint height on the map before uploading.
FlightHub 2: Wayline Library > Import, then assign the route to the device.

DJI Fly (no import function): create and save a placeholder waypoint mission on the controller, then replace its .kmz (Android/data/dji.go.v5/files/waypoint/<id>/<id>.kmz) with the exported file, keeping the placeholder's file name. Reopen the mission and review it before flying.
Take off from the planned takeoff point: all heights in the file are relative to the launch position.
formats.label: DJI WPML route (.kmz)

trigger_labels.distance: Distance interval (photo every N metres, set in the file)
trigger_labels.manual: None in the file (start interval shooting on the camera yourself)
trigger_labels.time: Time interval (photo every N seconds, set in the file)
trigger_labels.waypoint: Photo at every waypoint (one waypoint per photo; the aircraft stops for each)

formats.description: Mission plan for PX4 and ArduPilot vehicles, opened in QGroundControl and its derivatives.
instructions: QGroundControl: Plan view > File > Open, choose the .plan file, review it, then Upload to the vehicle.
Check that the firmware and vehicle type shown match your vehicle; the file states the planned ones.
Arm at the planned takeoff point: altitudes are relative to the home position.
formats.label: QGroundControl plan (.plan)

trigger_labels.distance: Distance interval (photo every N metres, set in the file)
trigger_labels.manual: None in the file (start interval shooting on the camera yourself)
trigger_labels.time: Time interval (photo every N seconds, set in the file)

formats.description: Plain-text mission (QGC WPL 110) read by Mission Planner, QGroundControl, MAVProxy and other MAVLink tools.
instructions: Mission Planner: Plan screen > Load File, choose the .waypoints file, review it, then Write.
QGroundControl: Plan view > File > Open also reads this format.
Arm at the planned takeoff point: altitudes are relative to the home position.
formats.label: MAVLink waypoint list (.waypoints)

trigger_labels.distance: Distance interval (photo every N metres, set in the file)
trigger_labels.manual: None in the file (start interval shooting on the camera yourself)
trigger_labels.time: Time interval (photo every N seconds, set in the file)

formats.description: Waypoint mission for the Litchi app (older DJI aircraft), imported in Litchi Mission Hub.
instructions: Litchi Mission Hub (flylitchi.com/hub): Missions > Import, choose the .csv file, review the route and heights on the map, then save it to your account.
In the Litchi app, open the saved mission in Waypoint mode and check the settings (finish action, heading mode, cruising speed) before starting: mission-level settings are not part of the CSV.
Take off from the planned takeoff point: altitudes are relative to the launch position.
formats.label: Litchi mission (.csv)

trigger_labels.distance: Distance interval (photo every N metres, set in the file)
trigger_labels.manual: None in the file (start interval shooting on the camera yourself)
trigger_labels.time: Time interval (photo every N seconds, set in the file)
trigger_labels.waypoint: Photo at every waypoint (one waypoint per photo; the aircraft stops for each)

formats.description: Only the survey area (or corridor centre line), for flight apps that import a boundary and plan their own flight lines.
instructions: Import the .kml as an area (or linear / corridor) mission in the aircraft's flight app, then set the height, overlap and speed there using the values from this plan.
DJI Pilot 2: Flight Route > Import Route (KMZ/KML), choose Mapping (or Linear Flight for a corridor). DJI GS RTK / GS Pro, WingtraPilot, eMotion and Autel's apps have an equivalent KML import.
The app plans its own flight lines: its line count, flight time and battery estimate replace the ones here.
formats.label: Survey boundary (.kml)

formats.description: Boundary, flight path, waypoints and takeoff point for Google Earth and briefings. Not flyable.
instructions: Open in Google Earth (or any KML viewer) to review the route against imagery and terrain.
This file is a picture of the plan. Do not load it into a flight app as a mission.
formats.label: Plan overview (.kml)

formats.description: Boundary, flight path and waypoints with their attributes, for GIS software and custom tooling.
instructions: Open in QGIS or any GIS; waypoint heights are metres above the takeoff point.
This file is data about the plan. It is not a mission file.
formats.label: Plan data (.geojson)

catalog.notice: Planning estimate only - not verified flight-safety information. Distances, times, photo counts, battery needs and terrain clearances are computed from nominal equipment data and elevation models and have not been checked against obstacles, airspace restrictions, NOTAMs, weather or the actual condition of the aircraft. The remote pilot is responsible for verifying the route on site and for complying with the applicable aviation rules.

params.help: Enter the flight height and read the resolution, or enter the resolution you need and read the height.
params.label: Plan by
params.name: altitude_from

params.help: Height above the takeoff point (constant altitude) or above the ground (terrain following).
params.label: Flight height
params.name: altitude_m

params.help: Size of one image pixel on the ground.
params.label: Ground resolution (GSD)
params.name: gsd_cm

params.help: Speed along the flight lines. Defaults to the aircraft's suggested mapping speed.
params.label: Flight speed
params.name: speed_ms

params.help: Overlap between consecutive photos along a flight line.
params.label: Front overlap
params.name: front_overlap

params.help: Overlap between neighbouring flight lines.
params.label: Side overlap
params.name: side_overlap

params.help: Compass bearing of the flight lines. Auto picks the direction that needs the fewest lines.
params.label: Flight direction
params.name: direction

params.help: How far each line continues past the boundary before turning. Automatic for the airframe when empty.
params.label: Line overshoot
params.name: overshoot_m

params.help: Fly a second grid at right angles to the first (better 3D reconstruction, about twice the flight).
params.label: Double grid
params.name: crosshatch

params.help: Corridor only: fly at least this many parallel passes even if one swath covers the width.
params.label: Minimum passes
params.name: corridor_min_passes

params.help: Auto starts at the corner nearest the takeoff point.
params.label: Start corner
params.name: start

params.help: Constant height above the takeoff point, or follow the terrain to keep the height above ground.
params.label: Altitude mode
params.name: altitude_mode

params.help: How far the flown height may differ from the ideal one between waypoints. Smaller follows more closely with more waypoints.
params.label: Terrain following tolerance
params.name: terrain_tolerance_m

params.help: Landscape puts the long side of the image across the flight line.
params.label: Camera orientation
params.name: camera_orientation

params.help: -90 looks straight down. Coverage estimates assume straight down.
params.label: Gimbal pitch
params.name: gimbal_pitch_deg

params.help: Exposure time as 1/x s; used to estimate motion blur at the chosen speed.
params.label: Shutter speed
params.name: shutter_speed

params.help: What the aircraft does after the last waypoint.
params.label: When finished
params.name: finish_action

params.help: Height above the takeoff point for the return flight. Defaults to the highest point of the mission.
params.label: Return height
params.name: rth_altitude_m

params.help: Speed to and from the survey area. Defaults to the mapping speed.
params.label: Transit speed
params.name: transit_speed_ms

params.help: Share of each battery kept in hand for the return and landing.
params.label: Battery reserve
params.name: reserve_percent

params.help: The plan is flagged where the estimated height above the terrain model falls below this.
params.label: Minimum terrain clearance
params.name: min_clearance_m

params.help: Height above ground of the tallest obstacle you know of in or near the area (trees, masts, cranes).
params.label: Tallest known obstacle
params.name: obstacle_height_m

params.help: Numeric limits the plan is compared with. Not legal advice.
params.label: Rule preset
params.name: regulation

params.help: Overrides the preset's limit, for example under a specific authorisation.
params.label: Height limit above ground
params.name: max_agl_m

params.help: Flag the plan when it goes further than this from the takeoff point.
params.label: Line-of-sight distance
params.name: vlos_m

rule_sets.label: Generic: 120 m above ground, visual line of sight
rule_sets.notes: The height limit most national rules share for operations without a specific authorisation.

rule_sets.label: EU / EASA Open category
rule_sets.notes: Open category: within 120 m of the closest point of the surface, in visual line of sight, under 25 kg. Subcategory, class marking and UAS geographical zones are not evaluated here.

rule_sets.label: USA / FAA Part 107
rule_sets.notes: 400 ft above ground level (higher only within 400 ft of a structure), 100 mph groundspeed, under 55 lb, visual line of sight. Airspace authorisation (LAANC) is not evaluated here.

rule_sets.label: Custom limits (specific authorisation)
rule_sets.notes: No preset limits: enter the limits of your authorisation in the plan.

assurance.summary: Within limits: speed, photo interval and height were compared with the DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise (M3E) and DJI Mavic 3E wide camera profiles, from published nominal specifications in the built-in catalog (2026-10). The profile is not the aircraft: firmware, payload and conditions change what it can do.
assurance.title: Aircraft and camera limits

assurance.summary: Estimated from Test DEM (30 m data, ±5 m nominal, sampled every 30 m). Lowest estimated height above it: 40 m. It models the ground only: trees, buildings, masts and wires are not in it. Treat the clearance as indicative and confirm it on site.
assurance.title: Terrain clearance

assurance.summary: Not checked. The platform has no data on trees, buildings, masts, cranes or power lines. Enter the height of the tallest obstacle you know of to compare the route with it, and inspect the site.
assurance.title: Obstacles

assurance.summary: Estimated: 45 min rated endurance x 0.8 (payload and real conditions) with 25% held in reserve gives 27 min usable per battery. Wind, temperature, battery age and hovering are not modelled.
assurance.title: Flight time and batteries

assurance.summary: Advisory: compared with 120 m above ground and 500 m from the takeoff point (Generic: 120 m above ground, visual line of sight). This is not legal advice and not an authorisation: registration, pilot competency, flights over people, night operations, permits and local rules are not evaluated.
assurance.title: Aviation rules

assurance.summary: Not checked. The platform holds no airspace data: controlled airspace, aerodromes, restricted and prohibited areas, temporary restrictions and NOTAMs must be checked with your aviation authority's official sources before every flight.
assurance.title: Airspace

assurance.summary: Not checked. Wind, gusts, temperature, precipitation and visibility are not considered; the DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise (M3E) is rated for winds up to 12 m/s. Headwind shortens endurance beyond the estimate.
assurance.title: Wind and weather

acknowledge.message: The ground rises to within 40 m of the flight height. Over the highest ground the overlap drops to about 50% front / 25% side and the resolution ranges 1.09-2.73 cm/px. Use terrain following or fly higher.
The route goes 614 m from the takeoff point, beyond the 500 m used here as a visual-line-of-sight distance. Plan observers, a closer takeoff point or the required authorisation.
